TOMORROW, SUNDAY — our last Anchorage pop-up of the year ❤️ fanniakbakery 
11 am - 4 pm 

If you told me a year ago that I’d still be doing more pop-ups in Anchorage, I wouldn’t have believed you. 😆
If y’all don’t know how hard it is to do a pop-up in a different city… you’re not prepping in your usual comfortable space, you’re buying gallons of milk, hauling everything, and doing it all over again. It’s a lot.
I wouldn’t normally put myself through that stress —
BUT YOU KNOW WHAT?
I love the stress, or the stress love me🤣
And the amazing support and love that YOU, Anchorage friends, show us is incredible 🥹❤️

I have no words. You make all the tiredness, the overwhelm, and the stress so worth it every single time.
Thank you for always showing up. See you tomorrow 🤍

Do you think batching matcha automatically means it’s lower quality? 🍵

🔗 Link in bio for our Substack on Batched Matcha Myths, Misconceptions, and Best Practices for Cafes and Pop-ups

Batched matcha is like the middle child of matcha, often misunderstood and overlooked 💔 Negative experiences with poorly handled batches have reinforced the stigma that batching = shortcuts or low quality compared to whisking to order.

But here’s the truth: both methods have their place in a cafe that manages a coffee and matcha program.

The real difference lies in systems and care. Many cafes hand whisk yet store matcha improperly or use water that’s too hot, resulting in oxidized, bitter drinks. The method itself isn’t the sole indicator of quality.

When done right, batching can produce consistently vibrant, smooth matcha every single time.
